scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows disputed bills for both estimated (1240) and actual (1785) read types, indicating that billing disputes are not solely driven by missing reads leading to estimation; actual reads also generate disputes, suggesting other error sources.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no tariff changes were made during the period; thus tariff changes are not a source of the dispute surge.

Field route completion for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual read routes are not being completed as planned, which can lead to missed reads, increased estimation, and consequently more billing disputes.
The observation shows dispute tickets rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming a sustained surge.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3.0 days), indicating that the surge in dispute tickets is not due to delayed responses.

U-U1.question: Which specific rule change(s) in the billing import/validation logic are causing the systematic bill errors?
U-U1.resolution_path: Conduct a detailed review of the billing-config change logs, isolate recent rule edits, test each in a staging environment, and deploy the corrected rule.
U-U1.safe_placeholder: Continue manual bill adjustments and monitoring while the investigation proceeds; maintain SLA‑compliant dispute handling.

U-U2.question: Will correcting the rule sufficiently reduce dispute volume to baseline, or do other factors (e.g., field staffing) also contribute?
U-U2.resolution_path: After rule correction, measure dispute volume trend over two full billing cycles; if volume remains elevated, investigate field‑staffing and route‑completion contributors.
U-U2.safe_placeholder: Maintain current manual dispute handling and SLA compliance; keep temporary work‑arounds (e.g., courtesy credits) in place.

U-U3.question: Is the pre‑August baseline of ~600 tickets/month still an appropriate target given seasonality or other external influences?
U-U3.resolution_path: Analyze historical dispute volumes (past 12‑24 months) to adjust the baseline for seasonality and any known billing‑cycle effects.
U-U3.safe_placeholder: Use a rolling 3‑month average as an interim target while the baseline is refined.
